v1.0.0 默认全屏 — TUI 默认全屏运行；设置 tuiMode: "regular" 可保留滚动回溯功能。文档
v0.99.2 默认暴露 codemode 的 MCP 服务器不再打乱 codemode 描述，也不会阻塞首次提示；工具可通过 searchTools() 发现。
v0.99.1 支持 OpenAI、Azure 和 OpenAI Codex 上的 GPT-6.1 Sol（Codex 新默认模型）。文档
v0.99.0 Codemode + MCP — 可连接 MCP 服务器并运行并行调用工具的 JavaScript。MCP 文档

3. 热门问题（按影响与参与度排名前10）

  1. #2870 — [已关闭] 遵循 XDG 基础目录规范（24条评论，63 👍） 长期存在的 Linux 用户体验问题：Pi 之前会在 $HOME 目录下生成大量文件。经过社区6个月的反馈后已解决。→

  2. #6665 — [开放中] 流式输出时 TUI 占满一个完整CPU核心（14条评论，6 👍） 严重性能退化：未缓存的 Intl.Segmenter + 逐块 Markdown 重建导致长会话中 CPU 占用率达100%。可在核心版本（pi -ne）中复现。当前最活跃的 Bug。→

  3. #8643 — [开放中] Bedrock：OpenAI 模型拒绝 toolResult.content 中的图片（10条评论） 供应商功能差距：Bedrock 上的 OpenAI 模型不会提取工具结果中的图片（openai-completions 支持该功能）。修复方案及测试已在 fork 仓库中就绪。→

  4. #10314 — [开放中] 重新考虑全屏模式下 Home/End 键的默认行为（9条评论，5 👍） v1.0.0 全屏版本将 Home/End 键从行编辑行为改为文档滚动行为。社区对默认行为的看法存在分歧。→

  5. #8301 — [开放中] 无法在队列中穿插执行压缩与提示请求（7条评论） 工作流 Bug：/compact 会取消会话，而不是在待处理提示之后排队执行。影响批量工作流。→

  6. #9134 — [开放中] Anthropic 适配器会移除工具 schema 顶层的 anyOf（6条评论） 隐蔽的正确性 Bug：带有顶层 anyOf 的自定义工具，其约束会在发送到 Anthropic 模型前被移除，导致无效的工具调用。→

  7. #10330 — [开放中] CLI 模式下自动压缩不启动（6条评论） 模式功能差距：pi --mode json 永远不会运行自动压缩，尽管 TUI 在 #6994 修复后已正常工作。→

  8. #9335 — [已关闭] 支持 configuration_update 以在保留缓存的情况下更改推理设置（5条评论，7 👍） GPT-6 优化请求：希望通过 configuration_update 调整推理强度且不破坏提示缓存。目前暂不处理，已关闭。→

  9. #10287 — [开放中] 网络错误后 getContextUsage() 估算值偏高（4条评论） 可靠性 Bug：可重试的 WebSocket/fetch 失败会导致上报的上下文使用量飙升（例如从42k涨至330k token）。→

  10. #10291 — [已关闭] MCP：将认证信息存储在密钥链中，而非 mcp-auth.json（3条评论） 安全改进请求：将 MCP 令牌从明文磁盘文件转移到系统密钥链。暂不处理，已关闭。→

4. 关键 PR 进展（前10）

  1. #9776 — 按思考层级设置采样参数（已合并 → v1.0.2） 实现了 samplingParamsByThinkingLevel，可为思考/非思考模式设置不同的采样参数。→

  2. #9137 — 添加 Nix flake（已合并 → v1.0.1） 新增 Nix flake 支持，可通过 nix run 一键运行/安装。→

  3. #10440 — 修复：每个进程仅解析一次 QuickJS wasm 路径（已合并） 修复了 #10439：执行 pnpm global update 后 codemode 失效的问题，原因是 wasm 路径在每次调用时都会重新解析。→

  4. #10383 — 性能优化（TUI）：对比原始行的指针相等性（已合并） 全屏 TUI 优化：未发生变化的行保留引用相等性，以减少重渲染。→

  5. #8734 — OpenAI Responses 供应商的顶层指令支持（开放中） 新增 systemPromptFormat 选项，可将系统提示移至顶层 instructions（避免重复，提升缓存命中率）。关闭了 #8388。→

  6. #9714 — 支持 Azure Foundry Chat Completions 部署（开放中） 将 Azure 供应商的支持范围从 Responses API 扩展到 Chat Completions 部署（例如 DeepSeek V4 Pro）。关闭了 #9645。→

  7. #10382 — 原生 llama.cpp 分类器模型支持（开放中） 通过 /v1/systemone 探测 llama.cpp 模型；决策模型（Julia-1、Laya 等）使用原生分类能力，而非回退到聊天模式。→

  8. #10410 — 暴露持久化思考、WebSocket、会话选项（开放中） 向持久化 ConversationStreamOptions 中添加了 thinkingBudgets、websocketConnectTimeoutMs 和 sessionId。→

  9. #10397 — 对重复使用的调用对去重工具调用 ID（已合并） 修复了当供应商重新发出参数修改后的相同 (call_id, id) 时，出现重复工具调用块的问题。→

  10. #10328 — 移除 Bedrock 上不匹配的思考块（已合并） 关闭了 #10324：使用 Bedrock thinking-binding-controls-2026-08-01 测试版功能移除过期思考块，而非返回400错误。→

5. 热门讨论

创意想法

  • #10128 — 能否添加禁用分享功能的选项？（2条评论，3 👍） 重新被提起的请求：希望提供分享功能的关闭开关，契合 Pi 的极简设计理念。→
  • #10126 — 让 GitHub 版本发布不可变？（2 👍） 供应链安全提议：固定发布产物，防止发布后被篡改。→
  • #10151 — 将工作记忆作为提示分段（任务 + 过往会话）（1条评论，1 👍） 提议将技能式懒加载扩展到任务状态和跨会话记忆。→
  • #5936 — 为什么不使用原生终端光标？（2条评论，2 👍） 关于 Pi 自定义反相块光标与终端原生光标的用户体验讨论。→

问答

  • #10446 — 为什么更新这么频繁？（1 👍） 社区对发布节奏突然加快（每天多次发布）的疑问。→
  • #10230 — Codemode 基准测试 / token 节省情况？（2条评论，1 👍） 将 codemode "仅代码"模式与英伟达 SoL-Pi "动作融合"研究进行对比的讨论。→

展示与分享

  • #10069 — agent-chat：独立 Pi 智能体的 P2P 消息传递（2条评论，1 👍） 无需编排器即可实现跨会话智能体协作（共享 Docker/端口/数据库）的扩展。→
  • #10447 — pi-durabletask-mcp：带引导与恢复功能的委派任务（1 👍） 扩展了 pi-delegate-mcp，支持基于 SQLite 的持久化任务以及 steer/follow_up 功能。→
  • #10432 — Threshold：以项目为根的多会话连续性测试框架（1 👍） 本地测试框架，通过检查点在独立的 Pi 工作会话间保留项目状态。→
  • #10331 — 为 Pi 微调的 Qwen 3.8 26B（1 👍） 社区分享的开源模型，专门为 Pi 智能体工作流做了微调。→

6. 功能请求趋势

  1. TUI 自定义与默认控制 — v1.0.0 全屏版本发布后，Home/End 键行为、原生光标、可主题化选择、分享功能开关、输出内边距一致性等都是大家最关心的问题。
  2. 跨模式功能对等 — CLI/JSON/RPC 模式在自动压缩、显示转换和队列管理方面落后于 TUI。
  3. 供应商与模型兼容性 — 扩展对 Azure（Foundry/Chat Completions）、Bedrock（图片处理、思考块）以及开源模型（llama.cpp 分类器、Qwen 微调版本）的支持。
  4. 安全与供应链加固 — 基于密钥链的 MCP 认证、不可变的 GitHub 版本发布、XDG 规范合规。
  5. 持久化与多智能体工作流 — 对跨会话记忆、委派任务、恢复功能和 P2P 智能体协作的需求不断增长。

7. 开发者痛点

  1. TUI 性能退化 — 全屏模式引入了 CPU 密集型流式输出（占满一个核心）和视觉故障（Windows 上视口跳转），是目前最活跃的 Bug 领域。
  2. 供应商间隐蔽的 schema/行为差异 — 工具 schema 被静默移除（Anthropic 的 anyOf）、图片处理缺口（Bedrock）、maxTokens 丢失（Codex），这些问题导致难以调试的失败。
  3. Codemode 脆弱性 — 包更新后路径解析失效，且 MCP 版本协商对不符合规范的服务器兼容性差。
  4. 压缩功能不一致 — 无法正确排队、CLI 模式下不运行、网络错误后上下文使用量上报不可靠。
  5. 扩展 API 缺口 — 缺少结构化日志、无法通过 ToolExecutionApi 执行嵌套工具、RPC 消费者缺少仅显示用的文本转换功能。
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code 社区动态摘要 | 2026-10-05

数据来源：github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code

1. 近7天亮点

本周Qwen Code v0.24.7稳定版正式发布，同时保持每日 nightly 构建更新，核心修复了代码模式（Code Mode）的文本对齐问题与权限处理逻辑。社区重点推进了托管智能体运行时的稳定性优化，解决了死锁、CI 偶发失败、会话生命周期相关缺陷，同时也在持续打磨 Kubernetes 运行时、后台 Shell/监控支持等实验性功能。

2. 版本发布

  • Qwen Code v0.24.7（稳定版）
    无破坏性变更。核心特性：在托管智能体模式下，绑定工作区的会话无需执行即可准入。
    发布链接

  • v0.24.7 nightly 构建（2026-09-29 至 2026-10-04）
    所有 nightly 构建均包含两项重复修复：

    1. fix(core)：结合惰性工具发现机制对齐 Code Mode 文本（PR #12990）
    2. fix(permissions)：正确遵循已批准的权限状态 最新 nightly 版本：v0.24.7-nightly.20261004.9915c7ff8f

  • SDK TypeScript v0.1.17
    捆绑了 CLI v0.24.7，与 SDK 基于同一源分支构建。
    发布链接

  • Qwen Code Desktop v0.24.7
    新增会话创建失败诊断信息留存能力，以及 Java SDK 托管运行时相关补充功能。
    发布链接

3. 热门问题

（按影响范围与社区参与度排名前10）

  1. #13333 [P1 缺陷] 普通硬件上≥8个并发轮次（Turn）出现停滞（锁护送）
    托管智能体存储路径中的严重并发缺陷，会导致会话数较高时吞吐量骤降。已通过新增的端到端测试框架复现问题。
    问题链接

  2. #13413 [P1 缺陷] 会话存储短暂中断会导致运行中轮次永久卡死
    数据库临时中断会造成会话日志写入永久失败，将瞬时故障转化为永久挂起，对托管部署场景影响严重。
    问题链接

  3. #13395 [特性] Kubernetes 工具运行时进度追踪
    追踪提案 #12389 下基于 Kubernetes 的工具运行时实现，包括可移植性与验收准入标准。6条评论显示跨团队正在积极协调推进。
    问题链接

  4. #9693 [已关闭缺陷] Windows 端 MCP 启动时报 -32000 连接错误
    已修复 Windows 桌面端即使禁用 MCP 仍会报 MCP 连接错误的问题，该问题曾影响 Windows 集成可靠性。共9条评论——为本周评论数最高的问题。
    问题链接

  5. #13415 [缺陷] 本地 Qwen3.x 模型被默认拥有1M上下文窗口
    对于上下文窗口更小（如262k）的本地部署场景，自动压缩机制永远不会触发，导致上下文触达上限时出现硬故障。
    问题链接

  6. #12878 [缺陷] Ollama 拒绝零参数工具（缺少 parameters 字段）
    由于 Qwen Code 省略了 properties 字段，Ollama 会对无参数工具返回400错误。1个点赞，4条来自本地部署用户的反馈评论。
    问题链接

  7. #13255 [缺陷] HostedWorkspaceToolTurnIT 中 CI 偶发失败
    Java SDK CI 流水线（MySQL 8.4 / Java 21）中的测试不稳定，会导致不相关 PR 出现误报构建失败，拖慢审核速度。
    问题链接

  8. #13392 [缺陷] Desktop/ACP 0.24.7 中 PreToolUse 的 updatedInput 被忽略
    该回归问题破坏了基于钩子的工具参数修改能力，阻塞了依赖传输层参数注入的 MCP 集成。是 #12922 的后续问题。
    问题链接

  9. #13280 [缺陷] 记忆发现机制会从父目录加载 QWEN.md/AGENTS.md
    配置文件会从 Git 根目录的上一级加载，这一异常行为破坏了 monorepo 场景下的项目隔离性。
    问题链接

  10. #13387 [缺陷] 自定义命令会将 @{...} 文件内容误判为模板语法
    被引用文件中的字面模板语法会被二次求值，导致自定义命令工作流中出现意外的变量替换。
    问题链接

4. 重点 PR 进展

（本周更新的影响力最高的10个 PR）

  1. #13289 feat(runtime): 实验性 Kubernetes CSI 运行时 + 持久化 Worker 确认
    将 Kubernetes 运行时从一次性临时会话扩展为 CSI 支持的持久化工作区，同时保留 Pod 身份持久化与授权状态。
    PR 链接

  2. #13265 feat(managed-agent): H3 后台 Shell 与监控运行时
    为托管智能体路径实现后台 Shell 执行与监控能力，配套双语设计文档已先行发布。
    PR 链接

  3. #13361 fix(managed-agent): 强化并诊断托管冷加载拒绝门控
    通过新增埋点与加固托管会话冷加载拒绝逻辑，解决 #13255 中 CI 偶发失败的问题。
    PR 链接

  4. #13299 fix(core): 在 models.dev 目录中支持带点号和短横线的模型 ID
    修复目录键值逻辑，兼容不同服务商的两种命名规范（如 glm-4-5v / glm-4.5v），解决模型查找失败问题。
    PR 链接

  5. #13400 feat(managed-agent): 有界审批输入预览
    为原生文件与 Shell 审批请求新增8192字节的有限预览能力，截断标识会通过公共 API 与 WebShell API 对外暴露。
    PR 链接

  6. #13179 fix(managed-agent): 强化托管面板故障生命周期 + Worker 路径 containment
    包含三项鲁棒性修复：托管运行时 Worker 的路径穿越防护、优化后的故障生命周期处理等。
    PR 链接

  7. #13219 fix(managed-agent): 用终止状态约束重试循环
    彻底消除托管智能体技术栈中的无限重试循环，新增重试预算与永久故障的终止状态处理机制。
    PR 链接

  8. #13250 fix(qqbot)!: 在线程作用域下恢复按组会话隔离
    QQ 机器人频道的破坏性修复：移除强制单会话覆盖逻辑，当 groupAllPolicy 设置为 keyword 或 all 时，恢复按组隔离能力。
    PR 链接

  9. #13276 fix(serve): 为冷加载409错误中的托管恢复拒绝分支命名
    将22个拒绝位点的通用 hosted_turn_recovery_required 错误码替换为细分标签，简化 CI 偶发失败的调试流程。
    PR 链接

  10. #13342 fix(web-shell): 托管会话 UI 正确性修复
    修复托管会话中的10个 UI 问题（2个严重问题，8个鲁棒性问题），包括错误横幅残留、轮次边界稳定状态异常等。
    PR 链接

5. 热门讨论

源材料未提供 GitHub Discussions 相关数据——本部分省略。

6. 特性需求趋势

  1. Kubernetes 原生运行时交付：对生产级容器化工具执行的需求强烈，目前在平台分发路线图中追踪。
  2. 托管智能体功能扩展：后台 Shell/监控、审批预览、更完善的多会话工作区处理是托管智能体路线图上的主流需求。
  3. 模型目录灵活性：用户希望支持动态推理强度档位，并更好地兼容不同服务商的变体模型 ID 命名格式。
  4. Web Shell 功能对齐：需求集中在记忆面板优化（自动记忆浏览、多语言支持），以匹配桌面端能力。
  5. CI/CD 可靠性提升：多条反馈要求减少测试不稳定问题，加快社区贡献 PR 的审核流转速度。

7. 开发者痛点

  1. 托管智能体并发与死锁缺陷：锁护送、间隙锁死锁、会话存储中断导致挂起等多个 P1/P2 问题，是生产环境最主要的摩擦来源。
  2. CI 不稳定：Java SDK 集成测试（尤其是 MySQL 流水线）的偶发失败会浪费开发者时间，延迟 PR 合并。
  3. 本地模型兼容性缺口：上下文窗口检测缺失、零参数工具参数省略、硬编码假设等问题，会破坏本地/Ollama 部署的工作流。
  4. 钩子系统回归：PreToolUse 钩子输出被忽略的问题，破坏了依赖运行时参数修改的扩展与 MCP 集成。
  5. 错误诊断不清晰：通用的409错误码与缺失的诊断上下文，导致托管会话故障在没有深入系统知识的情况下难以调试。

本周报由 agents-radar 自动生成。

AI CLI Tools Weekly Digest 2026-10-05

Cross-Tool Comparison

Cross-Tool AI CLI Ecosystem Comparison Report (2026-10-05 Community Digests)

1. Ecosystem Overview

The AI developer CLI tool ecosystem is in a high-velocity maturity phase, with all major vendors shipping rapid iterative releases (6–10 per week on average) focused on platform stability, plugin/extensibility systems, and enterprise-grade governance. A cross-industry shift toward agentic workflows is driving shared investment in subagent orchestration, context window management, and remote/headless operation, while Windows and cross-platform compatibility remain universal pain points. Open ecosystem standards like MCP (Model Context Protocol) are table stakes across every tool, with communities prioritizing interoperability between vendors and self-hosted model providers. Enterprise buyers are increasingly pushing for security hardening, audit trails, and organization-wide policy enforcement as these tools move from experimental to production-critical developer infrastructure.

2. Activity Comparison

Tool Hot Issues (Open/Total) Key PRs (Active) Hot Discussions Release Velocity (7d) Maturity Stage

3. Shared Feature Directions

Core requirements are converging across 70%+ of the tool ecosystems, indicating standardization of expected AI CLI capabilities:

  1. MCP compatibility & extensibility
    • All tools: Prioritizing MCP server stability, reconnection logic, and cross-platform lifecycle management.
    • Claude Code, Pi, Qwen Code: Investing in plugin/mod systems for deep engine behavior customization.
  2. Enterprise security & policy enforcement
    • Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, Qwen Code: Building organization-level permission ceilings, audit trails, and policy inheritance for user-installed plugins.
    • Gemini CLI, GitHub Copilot CLI: Hardening command injection guards and sandboxed execution for autonomous workflows.
  3. Context & cost control
    • All tools except Claude Code: Iterating on context compaction logic, with fixes for unbounded token retention, incorrect usage reporting, and infinite resend loops.
    • OpenCode, Pi: Adding configurable token retention limits and reset-time visibility for usage transparency.
  4. Cross-platform Windows reliability
    • All tools: Shipping Windows-specific bug fixes for ACL/sandbox setup, file lock conflicts, path handling, terminal UI rendering, and update lifecycle failures. Windows accounts for 30–40% of all high-priority issues across the ecosystem.
  5. Remote & headless operation
    • Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, GitHub Copilot CLI: Expanding remote control capabilities, daemon management, and mobile pairing support.
    • Qwen Code: Building Kubernetes-native runtime for hosted agent deployments.
  6. Subagent orchestration & observability
    • Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, OpenCode: Fixing subagent false success reporting, hangs, and adding visibility into running subagent status.
    • Pi, OpenAI Codex: Exploring cross-agent memory sharing and multi-agent coordination.

6. Trend Signals

For technical decision-makers and tool developers, these community patterns indicate industry-wide shifts to prioritize:

  1. Plugin systems are the new competitive battleground: The launch of Claude Mods and concurrent investment in extensibility across all tools signals that AI CLIs are evolving from point tools to platforms. Teams building for this ecosystem should prioritize MCP compatibility and structured plugin SDKs to capture ecosystem value.
  2. Enterprise security is no longer an afterthought: Organization-wide policy enforcement, audit trails, and sandbox hardening are appearing across every major tool, driven by enterprise buyer demand. Tools that lack native governance controls will be locked out of large enterprise procurement cycles in 2027.
  3. Windows compatibility remains a major quality differentiator: Across every tool, Windows-specific bugs account for a disproportionate share of high-priority issues. Teams that invest in first-class Windows testing and native platform integration will capture a significant user experience advantage.
  4. Context management is a critical unsolved problem: 6 of 7 tools are actively fixing context compaction bugs, incorrect usage reporting, and infinite loop issues. Accurate, configurable context window management will become a key purchasing criterion as agent workflows grow longer and more complex.
  5. Self-hosted and BYOK demand is accelerating: High community engagement around custom provider support, Ollama compatibility, and BYOK feature parity indicates that users want flexibility to mix and match models rather than being locked into a single vendor. Ecosystem tools that support multi-provider portability will see the fastest adoption.
  6. Agent reliability is the biggest barrier to adoption: Subagent hangs, false success reporting, and silent failures are top pain points across Gemini CLI, Qwen Code, and OpenCode communities. Building robust observability, error recovery, and guardrails for autonomous agent workflows will be critical to driving mainstream adoption of agentic coding tools.

3. Hot Issues

  1. #67609: Advisor tool unavailable on claude-fable-5 for transcripts >100K tokens
    The server-side advisor tool returns a hard error once Fable 5 conversations cross ~100K tokens, effectively disabling the feature for long-running sessions. It is the most-commented (27) and most-upvoted (45) open issue this week.

  2. #91763: Windows MSIX update blocked by surviving git fsmonitor daemon
    A git fsmonitor--daemon spawned by Claude Code inherits the AppX container job, survives forced update shutdowns, and blocks new version relaunches with error 0x80070020. The reporter includes root cause analysis and a no-reboot workaround.

    A previously working model selection broke abruptly for Windows desktop users, with 13 upvotes indicating broad impact. Affects users relying on Opus planning workflows.

  4. #98310: Remote control sessions hang after unarchive
    Server-mode claude remote-control sessions never get re-dispatched to the running host after being archived and unarchived from claude.ai, leaving messages stuck at "Sending…" before showing an offline error. Breaks long-running server workflow continuity.
    🔗 anthropics/claude-code#98310

  5. #98345: Auto permission mode drops on first session turn
    Sessions configured with defaultMode: "auto" often run the first turn in manual mode, only switching to auto after the desktop app re-sends the permission setting. Undermines automation expectations for fresh sessions.

    With two side-by-side Code chats open in the Windows desktop app, a mod’s AbovePrompt UI only appears in one chat, even though the mod runs in both. Degrades multi-session mod UX.

    A mod Pane with format: 'diff' shows raw diff text (no red/green shading, no line gutter, no word highlights) in the desktop app, while it renders correctly in the terminal. Creates UI parity gaps for mod developers.
    🔗 anthropics/claude-code#99535

  8. #99513: Stale MCP cache injects disconnected tools into all sessions
    A stale claudeAiMcpEverConnected cache entry in ~/.claude.json injects full tool definitions for 16 disconnected claude.ai MCP connectors into every CLI session, causing bloat and broken tool references.
    🔗 anthropics/claude-code#99513

  9. #71585: External-file-change system note asserts unverifiable cause
    The auto-generated note about file changes claims modification was done "by the user or by a linter" and implies user awareness, which the model then relays as fact — even when changes come from other processes. Risks misleading the model’s reasoning.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #99540: sec-default — org tool permission ceilings apply to user-installed plugins
    Enforces that organization-level tool approval/deny policies (via the policy mod) remain the effective ceiling even when users install third-party plugins. Every decision hook includes a .catch for fault tolerance.
    🔗 anthropics/claude-code#99540

  2. #99137: sec-default — plugins may only tighten, never loosen, inherited rules
    Complements #99540: user plugins can add stricter deny/ask rules or pin variables, but cannot relax policies set by the organization. Works with the existing published engine, no new API surface required.
    🔗 anthropics/claude-code#99137

  3. #40572: Add support for global Hookify rules
    Loads Hookify rules from the global ~/.claude/ directory in addition to project-level .claude/ rules, letting users enforce cross-repository hooks and standards without per-project configuration.

  4. #81672: fix(hookify) — decouple package import from install directory name
    Fixes Hookify plugin import failures when the plugin directory is not named exactly hookify (e.g., after marketplace installs with hashed directories). Resolves two linked bugs.
    🔗 anthropics/claude-code#81672

  5. #99206: diff — docked pane aligns header under engine head row
    Reduces excess blank space above the docked /diff pane header: the engine now reserves the top blank row for the pane’s close mark, eliminating redundant padding.
    🔗 anthropics/claude-code#99206

  6. #99141: diff — keep pane alive before it has content to render
    /diff opened before a host page attaches (or before any changes exist) now retains its pane slot, which populates automatically as soon as content is available, rather than failing silently.
    🔗 anthropics/claude-code#99141

  7. #99118: diff — allow toasts while the pane/dialog is open
    Removes the holdToasts: true behavior from /diff panes and dialogs. Other plugins’ transient toast notifications now display normally instead of being queued until the diff view closes.
    🔗 anthropics/claude-code#99118

  8. #94847: diff — only auto-open pane on first edit with a tracked file
    Stops the diff pane from opening empty when the first edit targets an ignored file, out-of-repo path, or different worktree. The pane now only opens when there is an actual tracked change to display.
    🔗 anthropics/claude-code#94847

  9. #98445: diff — read all file hunks in a single git process
    Replaces per-file git invocations (up to 50 per tool call) with a single process to read all changed hunks, drastically reducing process-spawn overhead — especially impactful on Windows, where process start is slower.

6. Feature Request Trends

  1. Plugin/mod system extensibility — Demand for global cross-project Hookify rules, richer mod UI APIs (selection context, diff rendering parity), and governance-focused plugins is accelerating as the Claude Mods ecosystem launches.
  2. Session organization & shared context — Users want sidebar groups to carry shared instructions and group-wide context across sessions, plus persistent group membership across restarts.
  3. CLI/desktop parity for advanced features — Consistent requests for diff formatting, mod UI elements, and MCP behavior to match between terminal, desktop app, and web surfaces.
  4. Mobile & headless workflow support — Growing interest in using Dispatch and remote-control sessions from mobile devices without requiring an always-on desktop host.
  5. Customizable UI chrome — Users want fine-grained control over status line elements (e.g., hiding mode indicators independently of hint text) to reduce redundancy for custom setups.

7. Developer Pain Points

  1. Windows platform instability — A cluster of high-impact Windows-specific bugs dominate issue activity: MSIX update failures from orphaned git processes, lost session groupings on reboot, VSCode OAuth race conditions in the credential store, and MCP native host copy failures.
  2. Permission mode & security policy gaps — Auto mode not activating on the first turn, plus ambiguity around how org policies interact with user-installed plugins, create trust and automation gaps for enterprise teams.
  3. Long-transcript reliability – The advisor tool failing outright on >100K token Fable 5 transcripts breaks core workflows for extended coding sessions and large-repo work.
  4. Desktop UI rendering inconsistencies — Multiple bugs around mod UI (AbovePrompt bands, diff formatting) only appearing in one chat or rendering incorrectly reduce confidence in mod development for desktop targets.
  5. Session lifecycle & remote control brittleness — Archived/unarchived remote sessions failing to re-dispatch, plus update restarts killing running sessions, disrupt long-running and headless workflows.
  6. Stale cache / state leakage — Injected stale MCP tools and incorrect file-change attribution notes introduce misleading state that can skew model behavior in hard-to-debug ways.

Maintainers also merged a batch of core performance and security improvements, including hardened subprocess argument handling on Windows and grep command injection mitigations.

4. Key PR Progress

  1. #29632 Bump npm-dependencies group (75 updates)
    P1 core dependency update including @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.23.0 → 1.30.1 and @octokit/rest 22.0.0 → 22.0.1, addressing upstream fixes and MCP compatibility.
  2. #29629 Cap pending plain text height to reduce streaming flicker
    Fixes full-screen clear/redraw flicker during streaming by capping MarkdownDisplay pending text height to terminal dimensions, directly addressing user reports of terminal flickering (#29628).
  3. #29536 Harden grep against command-line option injection
    Security fix for CWE-88: uses explicit -e pattern delimiters for both git grep and system grep to prevent argument injection via malicious search patterns.
  4. #29510 Harden Windows subprocess argument quoting
    Security fix for Windows: adds quoteCmdArg helper for shell: true invocations to prevent command injection in diff/editor subprocess calls.
  5. #29432 Settle queued tool calls on scheduler disposal
    Core reliability fix: rejects queued tool batches and cancels unstarted tools when the scheduler is disposed, avoiding orphaned approval requests and hangs.
  6. #29505 Support rootless Podman with keep-id
    P1 sandbox compatibility fix: correctly preserves host UID/GID in rootless Podman sessions, fixing sandbox startup failures for rootless container users.
  7. #29404 Add gemini models list with JSON output (CLOSED/merged)
    New feature: CLI subcommand for programmatic model discovery, eliminating hardcoded model IDs in integrations.
  8. #29411 Resolve resume latest to most recently active session (CLOSED/merged)
    UX fix: --resume now picks the most recently active session instead of the newest-created one, fixing cases where users resumed into stale short-lived sessions.
  9. #29626 Preserve shared references in JSON serialization
    Fix for safeJsonStringify: repeated non-circular object references (e.g., OTel metrics endTime) were incorrectly replaced with [Circular] due to a global seen WeakSet.
  10. #29517 Linearize array reconstruction in truncateHistoryToBudget
    Performance optimization: replaces O(n²) unshift()-based reordering with linear array building for history truncation, improving compression speed for long chat sessions.

No GitHub Discussions data was provided for this period.

6. Feature Request Trends

  1. AST-aware code tooling: Multiple linked issues (#22745, #22746, #22747) push for AST-powered file reads, search, and codebase mapping to reduce token usage, lower turn counts, and improve code navigation precision.
  2. Enhanced subagent observability & control: Users want subagent trajectories exposed via /chat share (#22598), bug reports that include subagent context (#21763), and better default use of custom skills/sub-agents (#21968).
  3. Browser agent hardening: Requests for settings override support (#22267), persistent session lock recovery (#22232), and Wayland compatibility (#21983) aim to make the browser agent production-ready across environments.
  4. Persistent, file-based task tracking: Replacement of in-context WriteToDo with CRUD-style filesystem-backed task tracking (#18836, #21000) to reduce context rot and preserve state across sessions.
  5. Sandboxing & safety guardrails: Demand for zero-dependency OS-level sandboxing (#19873), destructive operation guardrails (#22672), and rootless Podman support (#29505) to enable safe autonomous execution.
  6. Agent self-awareness: Requests for the CLI agent to accurately understand its own flags, hotkeys, and execution behavior (#21432) to act as a self-support tool.

7. Developer Pain Points

  1. Agent reliability regressions: Frequent hangs (generalist agent #21409, Vite app creation #22465) and false success reporting (#22323) erode trust in autonomous agent workflows, forcing users to disable subagents as a workaround.
  2. Poor subagent default behavior: The model fails to use installed skills and sub-agents unless explicitly prompted (#21968), reducing the value of custom agent ecosystems.
  3. Terminal UX friction: Streaming flicker (#29628, #21924), flaky selection list input (#29502), and broken resume session ordering (#29410) create day-to-day usability annoyances.
  4. Workspace hygiene issues: Scattered temporary scripts generated by the model (#23571) create cleanup overhead and clutter version control workspaces.
  5. Cross-platform compatibility gaps: Browser agent failures on Wayland (#21983), Windows subprocess quoting vulnerabilities (#29510), and rootless Podman breakage (#29505) fragment support across developer environments.
  6. Limited programmatic access: Lack of machine-readable model discovery (addressed by #29404) and symlink support for agent definitions (#20079) hinder integration with dotfiles and automation pipelines.
  7. Opaque error reporting: Silent ripgrep failures (#29552), missing subagent context in bug reports (#21763), and 400 errors with >128 tools (#24246) make debugging issues slow and difficult.

  • #10447 — pi-durabletask-mcp: delegated tasks with steering + recovery (1 👍) Extends pi-delegate-mcp with SQLite-backed durable tasks and steer/follow_up support. →
  • #10432 — Threshold: project-rooted harness for multi-session continuity (1 👍) Local harness that preserves project state across independent Pi worker sessions via checkpoints. →
  • #10331 — Qwen 3.8 26B fine-tuned for Pi (1 👍) Community-shared open model fine-tuned specifically for agentic Pi workflows. →

6. Feature Request Trends

  1. TUI customization & defaults control — Home/End key behavior, native cursor, themable selection, share-feature toggle, and output padding consistency are all top of mind post-v1.0.0 fullscreen.
  2. Cross-mode feature parity — CLI/JSON/RPC modes lag TUI on auto-compaction, display transforms, and queue management.
  3. Provider & model compatibility — Expanded Azure (Foundry/Chat Completions), Bedrock (image handling, thinking blocks), and open model (llama.cpp classifiers, Qwen fine-tunes) support.
  4. Security & supply-chain hardening — Keychain-based MCP auth, immutable GitHub releases, and XDG compliance.
  5. Durable & multi-agent workflows — Growing demand for cross-session memory, delegated tasks, recovery, and P2P agent coordination.

7. Developer Pain Points

  1. TUI performance regressions — Fullscreen mode introduced CPU-bound streaming (full core pinned) and visual glitches (viewport jumps on Windows), the most active bug area right now.
  2. Silent provider-specific schema/behavior differences — Tool schemas being silently stripped (Anthropic anyOf), image handling gaps (Bedrock), and dropped maxTokens (Codex) cause hard-to-debug failures.
  3. Codemode fragility — Path resolution breaks after package updates, and MCP version negotiation is brittle with non-conformant servers.
  4. Compaction inconsistency — Doesn't queue properly, doesn't run in CLI mode, and context-usage reporting is unreliable after network errors.
  5. Extension API gaps — No structured logging, no nested tool execution via ToolExecutionApi, and no display-only text transforms for RPC consumers.
Qwen Code — QwenLM/qwen-code

Qwen Code Community Digest | 2026-10-05

Data source: github.com/QwenLM/qwen-code

1. Last 7 Days' Highlights

This week saw the stable release of Qwen Code v0.24.7 alongside daily nightly builds, with core fixes for Code Mode text alignment and permission handling. The community prioritized stability work on the managed agent runtime, resolving deadlocks, CI flakes, and session lifecycle bugs while advancing experimental features like Kubernetes runtime and background Shell/Monitor support.

2. Releases

  • Qwen Code v0.24.7 (stable)
    No breaking changes. Key feature: workspace-bound sessions can be admitted without execution in managed agent mode.
    Release link

  • v0.24.7 nightly builds (2026-09-29 to 2026-10-04)
    All nightly builds include two recurring fixes:

    1. fix(core): Align Code Mode text with lazy tool discovery (PR #12990)
    2. fix(permissions): Honor approved permission states Latest nightly: v0.24.7-nightly.20261004.9915c7ff8f

  • SDK TypeScript v0.1.17
    Bundles CLI v0.24.7, built from the same source branch as the SDK.
    Release link

  • Qwen Code Desktop v0.24.7
    Includes session creation failure diagnostic preservation and Java SDK managed runtime additions.
    Release link

3. Hot Issues

(Top 10 by impact and community engagement)

  1. #13333 [P1 Bug] ≥8 concurrent Turns stall on modest hardware (lock convoy)
    Critical concurrency bug in managed agent store path causes throughput collapse at high session counts. Reproduced via new E2E test harness.
    Issue link

  2. #13413 [P1 Bug] Transient Session Store outage permanently wedges running Turns
    A temporary database outage breaks session log writes permanently, turning transient failures into permanent hangs. High severity for hosted deployments.
    Issue link

  3. #13395 [Feature] Kubernetes tool runtime progress tracker
    Tracks implementation of Kubernetes-based tool runtime under proposal #12389, including portability and acceptance gates. 6 comments indicating active cross-team coordination.
    Issue link

  4. #9693 [Closed Bug] Windows MCP -32000 connection error at startup
    Fixed issue where Windows desktop reported MCP connection errors even when MCP was disabled, affecting Windows integration reliability. 9 comments — highest comment count this week.
    Issue link

  5. #13415 [Bug] Local Qwen3.x models assumed to have 1M context window
    Auto-compaction never triggers for local deployments with smaller context windows (e.g. 262k), causing hard failures when context limits are hit.
    Issue link

  6. #12878 [Bug] Ollama rejects zero-argument tools (missing parameters field)
    Ollama returns 400 errors for tools with no arguments because Qwen Code omits the properties field. 1 upvote, 4 comments from users hitting this in local deployments.
    Issue link

  7. #13255 [Bug] Intermittent CI failure in HostedWorkspaceToolTurnIT
    Flaky test in Java SDK CI lane (MySQL 8.4 / Java 21) causes false red builds on unrelated PRs, slowing down review velocity.
    Issue link

  8. #13392 [Bug] PreToolUse updatedInput ignored in Desktop/ACP 0.24.7
    Regression breaking hook-based modification of tool arguments, blocking MCP integrations that rely on transport argument injection. Follow-up to #12922.
    Issue link

  9. #13280 [Bug] Memory discovery loads QWEN.md/AGENTS.md from parent directory
    Unexpected behavior where configuration files are loaded from one level above the git root, breaking project isolation for monorepo setups.
    Issue link

  10. #13387 [Bug] Custom commands misinterpret @{...} file content as template syntax
    Literal template syntax inside referenced files gets re-evaluated, causing unintended variable substitution in custom command workflows.
    Issue link

4. Key PR Progress

(Top 10 most impactful PRs updated this week)

  1. #13289 feat(runtime): Experimental Kubernetes CSI runtime + durable worker ACK
    Extends Kubernetes runtime from disposable scratch sessions to CSI-backed persistent workspaces, with Pod identity persistence and authorization preservation.
    PR link

  2. #13265 feat(managed-agent): H3 background Shell and Monitor runtime
    Implements background shell execution and monitoring for the managed agent path, with bilingual design docs shipped first.
    PR link

  3. #13361 fix(managed-agent): Harden and diagnose Hosted cold-load refusal gates
    Addresses the intermittent #13255 CI failure by adding instrumentation and hardening cold-load rejection logic for hosted sessions.
    PR link

  4. #13299 fix(core): Support dotted + dashed model IDs in models.dev catalog
    Fixes catalog keying to handle both spelling conventions (e.g. glm-4-5v / glm-4.5v) across providers, resolving model lookup failures.
    PR link

  5. #13400 feat(managed-agent): Bounded approval input previews
    Adds 8192-byte bounded previews for native file and Shell approval requests, with truncation flags exposed via public and WebShell APIs.
    PR link

  6. #13179 fix(managed-agent): Harden managed panel failure lifecycle + worker path containment
    Three robustness fixes including path traversal protection for managed runtime workers and improved failure lifecycle handling.
    PR link

  7. #13219 fix(managed-agent): Bound retry loops with terminal states
    Eliminates infinite retry loops across the managed agent stack, adding retry budgets and terminal state handling for permanent failures.
    PR link

  8. #13250 fix(qqbot)!: Restore per-group session isolation under thread scope
    Breaking fix for QQ Bot channel: removes forced single-session override, restoring per-group isolation when groupAllPolicy is set to keyword or all.
    PR link

  9. #13276 fix(serve): Name Hosted recovery-refusal branches in cold-load 409s
    Replaces generic hosted_turn_recovery_required error codes with granular labels across 22 refusal sites, simplifying CI flake debugging.
    PR link

  10. #13342 fix(web-shell): Managed session UI correctness fixes
    Fixes 10 UI issues in managed sessions (2 critical, 8 robustness), including stale error banners and Turn-boundary settle state bugs.
    PR link

5. Hot Discussions

No GitHub Discussions data was provided in the source material — section omitted.

6. Feature Request Trends

  1. Kubernetes-native runtime delivery: Strong demand for production-grade containerized tool execution, tracked under the platform-distribution roadmap.
  2. Managed agent feature expansion: Requests for background shell/monitoring, approval previews, and better multi-session workspace handling dominate the managed agent roadmap.
  3. Model catalog flexibility: Users want dynamic reasoning effort tiers and better support for variant model ID spellings across providers.
  4. Web Shell feature parity: Requests for memory panel improvements (auto-memory browsing, locale support) to match desktop capabilities.
  5. Improved CI/CD reliability: Multiple requests to reduce flaky tests and speed up PR review turnaround for community contributions.

7. Developer Pain Points

  1. Managed agent concurrency and deadlock bugs: Multiple P1/P2 issues around lock convoys, gap-lock deadlocks, and session store outages causing hangs are the top source of production friction.
  2. CI flakiness: Intermittent failures in Java SDK integration tests (especially MySQL lanes) waste developer time and delay PR merges.
  3. Local model compatibility gaps: Missing context window detection, omitted zero-argument tool parameters, and hardcoded assumptions break workflows with local/Ollama deployments.
  4. Hook system regressions: PreToolUse hook output being ignored breaks extension and MCP integrations that rely on runtime argument modification.
  5. Unclear error diagnosis: Generic 409 error codes and missing diagnostic context make hosted session failures hard to debug without deep system knowledge.

This weekly digest is auto-generated by agents-radar.

OpenClaw 生态周报 2026-10-05

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | 覆盖项目: 5 个 | 生成时间: 2026-10-05 01:47 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw 项目深度报告

OpenClaw 项目周报（2026-10-05）

数据来源： github.com/openclaw/openclaw 统计周期： 截至 2026-10-05 的 7 天

1. 近 7 天整体概况

本周 OpenClaw 保持高速开发节奏，共更新 500 个 issue（350 个活跃中，150 个已关闭）和 500 个 PR（309 个开放中，191 个已合并/关闭）。项目发布了 5 个新版本，包括 1 个新稳定版和多个扩展稳定版（相当于 LTS）的网关更新，体现了活跃的功能开发与持续的安全/可靠性维护并重。

核心工作重点包括更新管道可靠性、状态与会话管理的性能优化，以及多智能体和渠道集成 bug 修复。社区参与度持续走高，围绕成本治理、内存系统改进、多智能体权限范围等话题讨论热烈。项目整体健康度良好，bug 修复与前瞻性功能开发稳步推进。

2. 版本发布

本周共发布 5 个新版本，覆盖稳定版和扩展稳定版渠道：

v2026.9.8（稳定版）

  • 数据： 58 次提交、43 个 PR、21 位贡献者
  • 详情： 最新稳定版，完整变更日志见官方发布说明
  • 链接： openclaw/openclaw Release v2026.9.8

v2026.9.7（稳定版）

  • 数据： 518 次直接提交、2818 个 PR、334 位贡献者
  • 详情： 重要稳定版，包含大量功能更新与 bug 修复；发布说明见官方文档
  • 链接： openclaw/openclaw Release v2026.9.7

扩展稳定版（仅网关）（相当于 LTS）

基于 2026 年 8 月基线发布了 3 个扩展稳定版更新，重点为安全补丁、可靠性修复、性能优化和新模型支持：

  • v2026.8.35：openclaw/openclaw Release v2026.8.35
  • v2026.8.34：openclaw/openclaw Release v2026.8.34
  • v2026.8.33：openclaw/openclaw Release v2026.8.33

现有发布数据中未提及破坏性变更或强制迁移步骤。

3. 项目进展

在本周合并/关闭的 191 个 PR 中，核心进展如下：

更新与安装可靠性

  • PR #165257： 修复非特权容器中 openclaw update 失败的问题——当 FICLONE ioctl 被拒绝时回退到字节拷贝方式（解决 #164113）
  • PR #165242： 修复相同包更新时的旧配置处理逻辑，避免准入后配置被拒绝
  • PR #165233： 修复原地更新成功后，因清理代码导入过时导致的 CLI 误报错误

性能优化

  • PR #165249： 消除冗余消息跳转，降低 worker 任务传输的持续开销
  • PR #165186： 通过细化 SQLite 持有警告归因和复用完整性证明，提升共享状态性能
  • PR #165221： 限制对话记录源读取量，防止大型会话历史操作时出现 100MB 以上的堆内存峰值

Bug 修复

  • PR #165210： 修复 Code Mode 中，当提供商在多个响应中复用工具调用 ID 时导致的嵌套调用失败问题
  • PR #142888： 修复兼容 OpenAI 的提供商在增量消息中重发完整内容时，实时助手文本重复的问题（解决 #136262）
  • PR #144488： 让内存嵌入请求超时可配置且支持恢复，修复慢提供商导致的索引永久卡顿问题

UI/UX 改进

  • PR #164607： 在个人资料 UI 中为网关管理员新增渠道身份链接管理功能
  • PR #165199： 修复侧边栏固定编辑器与排序把手控件重叠的问题

4. 社区热门话题

本周讨论最活跃的 issue 反映了用户在成本控制、运行时稳定性和内存系统行为方面的核心诉求：

  1. 网关层面按智能体实施成本预算管控

    • Issue： #42475（25 条评论，1 👍）
    • 分析： 运维人员希望在网关层面为每个智能体设置原生的日/月成本上限，无需外部监控工具即可避免费用失控。这解决了多智能体部署中的核心运维痛点——当前按会话跟踪的方式无法提供主动的预算防护。

  2. 钩子/工具执行导致僵尸子进程泄漏

    • Issue： #97616（17 条评论，1 👍）
    • 分析： 用户反馈 openclaw-hooks、bash 和 codex 子进程不断累积且未被回收，随时间推移会降低运行时性能。对于长期运行的网关实例，这是高优先级稳定性问题。

  3. 短期记忆保留驱逐机制阻碍记忆升级

    • Issue： #150635（17 条评论，0 👍）
    • 分析： 当短期记忆达到 512 条上限后，夜间“深度梦境”阶段无法将记忆升级到长期存储，原因是每晚都会摄入零回忆条目。对于高会话量的用户，这破坏了内存系统的核心功能。

  4. 内存核心表中 SQLite 无限制增长

    • Issue： #114612（16 条评论，0 👍）
    • 分析： memory_index_chunks 和 memory_embedding_cache 表无限制增长，存在磁盘耗尽风险。对于长时间运行的生产部署，这是关键持久性问题。

5. Bug 与稳定性

本周报告/更新的 bug 按严重程度（P0 > P1 > P2）和影响排序：

P0（严重）

  1. #164396： 在全新安装 Windows 11 + Node 22 LTS 的环境中，OpenClaw 2026.9.8 无法连接本地网关
    • 影响：新 Windows 用户上手失败；暂无修复 PR
  2. #160959： 捕获大型外部插件时网关阻塞数分钟（2026.9.6 引入的回归）
    • 影响：事件循环饥饿；暂无修复 PR
  3. #157415： doctor --fix 拒绝对外部安装的 acpx 和 codex 执行会话后插件迁移
    • 影响：插件用户迁移失败；暂无修复 PR
  4. #158390： plugin-captures 临时目录未被垃圾回收，持续占用磁盘
    • 影响：磁盘耗尽；社区支持 1 👍；暂无修复 PR

P1（高优先级）

  1. #97616： 钩子/工具导致僵尸子进程泄漏（见社区热门话题）
  2. #114612： 内存 SQLite 表无限制增长（见社区热门话题）
  3. #161379： 因 OpenAI 目录刷新循环（60 秒 TTL 短于单智能体刷新时间），网关 CPU 核心持续满载
    • 影响：单核心 100% CPU 占用；暂无修复 PR
  4. #161976： 重启后 WhatsApp 私信回复在持久化注册交接时失败
    • 影响：消息丢失；暂无修复 PR
  5. #144291： 配置热重载会中止所有进行中的智能体轮次
    • 影响：会话中断；暂无修复 PR

值得关注的回归问题

  • #97616（僵尸进程）：相较早期版本的回归
  • #161379（CPU 满载）：2026.9.6 引入的回归
  • #160959（插件捕获阻塞）：2026.9.6 引入的回归

6. 功能需求与路线图信号

最受用户需求、且大概率纳入路线图的功能：

  1. 按智能体实施成本预算管控（#42475）

    • 在网关层面为每个智能体设置日/月支出上限。对企业部署具有很高运维价值；鉴于讨论活跃且已被维护者标记评审，大概率会被优先安排。

  2. 按智能体设置 agentToAgent 和会话可见性范围（#59149）

    • 将全局唯一的多智能体权限设置替换为按智能体范围配置。已获得 2 👍 反应，且有相关 PR（相关 issue 中引用了 #155442），是即将发布版本的有力候选。

  3. 共享工作区内存索引（#95724）

    • 按源目录而非智能体索引内存，避免同一工作区下多个智能体重复存储向量库。可提升性能并减少资源占用，契合当前内存系统优化方向。

  4. Swarm agents.run 的受限启动契约（#156632）

    • 为 Swarm 智能体验证通道添加受限执行边界。已有关联实现 PR（#155442），表明正在积极开发中。

7. 用户反馈总结

痛点

  • 更新可靠性： 多平台出现更新失败、回滚和安装卡住的问题（macOS 非 root #164422、Windows 全新安装 #164396、非特权容器 #164113）。
  • 资源泄漏： 插件捕获导致的磁盘和内存泄漏 #158390、内存表增长 #114612 以及僵尸进程 #97616，是长期部署中的反复出现的问题。
  • 渠道投递问题： WhatsApp #161976、Signal #143581、iMessage #143632 和 Telegram #143278 上的消息丢失和投递失败，影响核心用户信任。
  • 多智能体使用障碍： 权限范围 #59149、子智能体投递失败 #143334 以及 claude-cli 多智能体 bug #164972，阻碍了团队型智能体工作流的普及。

使用场景

  • 具备成本治理和分层权限模型的企业多智能体部署
  • 跨多个聊天渠道、用于个人/团队生产力的长期自托管网关
  • 基于 Codex 和 claude-cli 后端的 Code Mode 与开发自动化
  • 用于知识工作和长期项目上下文的记忆增强智能体

满意度信号

  • 社区贡献活跃（每个版本有 21-334 位贡献者），表明用户参与度高
  • 回归 bug 分类处理迅速（多个 2026.9.x 回归问题已得到即时关注）

8. 待办关注

需要维护者关注的长期存在或高影响 issue/PR：

  1. #84037： 优化 Codex 应用服务器稳态 CPU 占用和辅助进程开销

    • 创建时间：2026-05-19；11 条评论，1 👍；P1 优先级。影响 Codex 用户的性能问题，暂无修复 PR。

  2. #95724： 按源目录而非智能体索引内存

    • 创建时间：2026-06-22；6 条评论，1 👍；P2 优先级。针对多智能体工作区的效率改进，暂无关联 PR。

  3. #59149： 按智能体设置 agentToAgent 和会话可见性范围

    • 创建时间：2026-04-01；6 条评论，2 👍；P2 优先级。已有关联 PR 但仍处于开放状态，等待产品决策。

  4. #119055： fix(code-mode): keep waiting results durable across retries

    • 创建时间：20

横向生态对比

跨项目个人AI助手/智能体开源生态对比报告

报告周期：截至2026-10-05的7天

1. 生态概述

开源个人AI助手与智能体生态仍处于高速增长、快速迭代阶段，各项目同时推进基础可靠性建设，以及面向企业和高级用户部署的需求驱动型功能拓展。本次调研的五个项目中，核心投入方向包括运行时稳定性、内存系统优化、多渠道集成，以及多智能体部署的成本管控。社区贡献率保持强劲，新贡献者在各层级项目中均提供了针对性修复与功能补充，而安全加固与沙箱机制仍是生产级部署不可妥协的优先级。当前生态按使用场景划分为三类：通用网关型平台、本地优先的轻量智能体、工作流优化型助手，分别面向不同用户群体与部署模式。

2. 活跃度对比

3. OpenClaw的市场定位

OpenClaw是本次调研范围内明显的市场与成熟度领跑者，其Issue与PR体量是排名第二梯队项目的10倍，拥有完善的多渠道发布管线（稳定版+扩展稳定版/LTS），且贡献者基数最大（每个版本贡献者数量在21–334人之间）。它采用网关为核心的技术路线，优先发展多智能体编排、跨渠道集成，以及企业级运营管控能力（成本治理、权限范围控制），这些能力在同类项目中仍处于起步阶段。 与规模更小的同类项目相比，OpenClaw拥有更成熟的企业用户基础，这体现在社区对生产可扩展性、成本控制、长期部署可靠性的关注上；而Hermes Agent与QwenPaw更侧重终端用户体验与前端打磨，IronClaw聚焦安全优先的沙箱执行，ZeroClaw则瞄准本地优先、注重隐私的部署场景。

4. 共同技术关注方向

  1. 运行时稳定性与资源泄漏治理 全项目共性优先级：五个项目均存在内存泄漏、进程泄漏或事件循环阻塞相关的待解决问题。OpenClaw报告了僵尸子进程泄漏与SQLite内存表无限制增长问题；QwenPaw记录了因流式缓冲区无限制导致的每秒1MB内存增长问题；ZeroClaw正在解决SQLite会话后端效率问题；Hermes Agent提到了WebSocket重连循环导致的CPU占满问题；IronClaw在跟踪基准测试管线的稳定性缺陷。
  2. 安装/更新可靠性 OpenClaw、Hermes Agent与ZeroClaw均报告了平台特定的安装失败问题：OpenClaw修复了非特权容器更新失败与Windows全新安装的连接问题；Hermes Agent记录了Termux/ARM64与Windows平台Python 3.14环境下的更新崩溃问题；ZeroClaw提到了Android/Termux快速入门流程失败的问题。
  3. 聊天/对话记录体验可靠性 Hermes Agent、QwenPaw与OpenClaw均优先修复流式输出与对话记录完整性Bug：Hermes Agent解决了桌面端消息重复渲染与滚动跳变问题；QwenPaw处理了压缩历史加载失败与跨会话消息归属错误问题；OpenClaw修复了兼容OpenAI的服务商下实时助手文本重复问题。
  4. 插件/工具系统健壮性 OpenClaw、Hermes Agent、QwenPaw与IronClaw均有正在推进的插件可靠性工作：OpenClaw修复了插件捕获磁盘泄漏与迁移失败问题；Hermes Agent处理了并发加载插件导致的崩溃问题；QwenPaw解决了插件同步调用冻结问题；IronClaw正在推进Turn-0工具选择优化。

6. 社区动能与成熟度

第一梯队：成熟、高迭代速度（稳定化+功能拓展并行）

  • OpenClaw：成熟度最高的项目，安全补丁、Bug修复与前瞻性功能开发节奏均衡。其稳定版/扩展稳定版双发布管线，以及每周191个PR的合并量，体现了成熟的发布工程能力与充足的维护者资源。项目处于持续增长阶段，在推进可靠性加固的同时，优先发展企业运营相关功能。

第二梯队：中等成熟度、活跃开发（功能优先迭代）

  • QwenPaw：迭代节奏稳定，聚焦前端体验与服务商/渠道兼容性。其测试版发布节奏与每周11个PR的合并量，反映出项目在处理Bug的同时积极推进功能开发，首次贡献者带来的社区贡献持续增长。
  • Hermes Agent：PR待合并与已合并比例较高，说明项目正处于活跃开发周期，重点聚焦桌面体验与工作流功能，暂无即将发布的稳定化版本。社区对跨设备连续性与看板可靠性的强烈需求是路线图的核心驱动力。
  • IronClaw：活跃度体量较小但稳定，工作内容涵盖安全补丁发布、依赖维护与早期架构研发。外部贡献者参与度提升表明社区认可度不断扩大，其对沙箱安全的聚焦使其成为小众但高信任度的选择。

第三梯队：预稳定阶段、基础加固

  • ZeroClaw：大量高优先级Bug与架构类增强需求仍在推进中，说明项目仍在为v0.8.6与v0.9.0里程碑夯实基础可靠性。其对本地优先隐私与运行时安全的聚焦吸引了小众用户群体，但合并速度较慢、多个功能处于搁置状态，说明维护者资源少于第一/第二梯队项目。

7. 趋势信号

  1. 企业运营管控能力已成为生产落地的必备条件 OpenClaw社区最受关注的需求是网关级的单智能体成本预算，加上对单智能体权限范围控制的需求，表明多智能体部署正从试点走向生产，需要原生治理工具而非外部监控的临时方案。面向企业场景的AI智能体开发者应优先内置成本上限、审计日志与细粒度权限模型。
  2. 本地优先与隐私导向的部署需求加速增长 ZeroClaw的local_small运行时配置需求极高，加上用户对本地模型下提示词冗余、内部指令泄漏的不满，反映出市场对针对本地部署与消费级硬件优化的轻量、隐私保护型智能体模式的需求正在增长。开发者应针对本地部署目标优化提示词体积，并禁用不必要的宽松降级策略。
  3. 跨设备、跨渠道连续性是核心体验差异化点 Hermes Agent的CLI与桌面端无缝切换功能、QwenPaw的移动端Web适配工作、OpenClaw的多渠道集成修复，均表明用户期待智能体能够在不同设备与聊天平台间无缝访问。仅支持单一接口的智能体在2026年将面临越来越大的体验竞争压力。
  4. 内存系统的可靠性与可扩展性是尚未解决的核心痛点 OpenClaw的短期内存淘汰Bug与SQLite无限制增长问题，加上QwenPaw的压缩历史加载失败问题，表明当前内存架构无法满足高负载、长期运行的部署需求。智能体开发者应优先实现有界内存存储、历史对话分页，以及可靠的长期记忆升级管线。
  5. 用户对沙箱安全的预期已超出现有实现水平 IronClaw对WASM沙箱加固的聚焦、ZeroClaw的macOS Seatbelt Bug修复，以及Hermes Agent用户对未沙箱化的browser_exec代码的意外反馈，都说明用户默认预期的安全边界强于多数项目当前的实际能力。清晰透明的沙箱范围文档，以及工具执行路径的一致安全管控，是建立用户信任的关键。

Hermes Agent — nousresearch/hermes-agent

Hermes Agent 项目周报 | 2026-10-05

1. 过去7天概览

过去一周Hermes Agent项目保持高强度开发节奏，共更新50个Issue（46个待处理，4个已关闭）和50个Pull Request（44个待处理，6个已合并/关闭），无新版本发布。工作重点集中在桌面端流式传输稳定性修复、插件加载、安装/打包流程以及看板工作流正确性优化，同时针对性新增了跨设备会话流转和仪表盘用户体验改进功能。待处理与已关闭工作项的比例表明，项目正处于活跃开发周期，有多条改进线并行推进，而非发布前的稳定阶段。维护者的优先级明显向兼容性和安装/更新可靠性倾斜，多个来自社区的包管理和平台特定修复PR已被纳入待处理队列，等待最终审核。

2. 版本发布

过去7天未发布新版本。

3. 项目进展

以下已合并/关闭的PR在过去一周交付了完整功能和修复：

  • 桌面端消息重复渲染修复 (PR #130448)：解决了Issue #130396中描述的问题——在桌面端对话记录里，包含Markdown表格的助手回复在工具调用后会渲染两次。该修复调整了流式消息气泡的落定逻辑，改用工具调用后的最终回复内容，而非重新绘制已有内容。
  • 桌面端流式消息气泡终态修复 (PR #128873, 已关闭)：解决了助手回复重复的根本原因——将补全内容落定到最后一个带有文本的助手消息气泡上，避免工具调用后的空白气泡接收重复内容。
  • 另有4个已关闭的PR（包含Bug修复和无效/重复条目）完成了本周的合并/关闭队列，其中大部分关闭项针对桌面客户端流式传输稳定性。

4. 社区热点话题

讨论最活跃的事项反映了用户对客户端用户体验Bug、插件/安装可靠性痛点的不满：

  1. 桌面端对话记录重复 + 流式传输时滚动跳变 (Issue #128468, 13条评论, 1 👍)：本周互动量最高的Issue，由一位使用v0.21.5版本的Linux桌面用户上报。核心诉求是可靠、无卡顿的流式用户体验——重复消息和滚动跳变破坏了聊天的核心可用性，也削弱了用户对对话记录准确性的信任。
  2. 插件并发加载崩溃："dictionary changed size during iteration" (Issue #125746, 6条评论)：影响运行时间长、插件数量多的安装环境，表现为间歇性故障，会静默丢失已注册的工具。用户需要在重度定制场景下拥有稳健的并发插件发现机制，避免功能静默丢失。
  3. 看板调度器Worker出现ModuleNotFoundError崩溃 (Issue #125649, 6条评论)：在受管Python运行环境下，看板功能完全不可用。依赖看板进行任务委派的用户需要Worker在不同运行环境中保持一致的启动行为。

5. Bug与稳定性

过去一周上报/更新的Bug，按严重程度排序（P1 > P2 > P3）：

P1（严重）

  • 上下文压缩流转内容被重新发布为助手回复 (Issue #132934)：在长时间CLI会话中，上下文压缩内容会被当作实时助手回复展示，开头带有改写内容，绕过了摘要分类。目前暂无关联修复PR；该问题会破坏会话连贯性，可能误导用户对智能体实时输出的判断。

P2（高影响）

  • OpenAI-Codex会话中途模型切换静默失败 (Issue #132935)：执行/model --provider openai-codex命令显示成功，但实际未绑定实时API客户端，导致下一条消息返回403错误。暂无关联修复PR。
  • SSH远程配置回归 (Issue #88994)：当本地配置名与远程remoteProfile不一致时，SSH连接会断开，这是commit 30299efa3引入的回归问题。暂无关联修复PR。
  • Bot模式 / Bot间投递缺少ruamel模块 (Issues #125091, #125654)：在负载解释器上启动的投递运行器缺少PM依赖目录，导致持续失败。暂无关联修复PR。
  • 自定义提供商身份不同步 (Issue #102725)：两个共享base_url但api_mode不同的自定义提供商，始终只会解析到第一个条目，造成展示/运行时不匹配。暂无关联修复PR。
  • 仪表盘WebSocket无限重连循环 (Issue #132999)：短暂的连接断开会触发250ms周期的重连循环，导致CPU占用率达到100%，这是PR #95951附近引入的回归问题。暂无关联修复PR。
  • hermes prompt-size执行未文档化的网络调用 (Issue #132998)：尽管文档说明该命令为离线运行，但实际会获取OpenRouter的模型列表，违背了用户对纯本地运行的预期。暂无关联修复PR。

P3（中/低影响）

  • 磁盘清理插件对tracked.json的竞争条件 (Issue #132943)、Home Assistant插件过度迁移 (Issue #132814) 以及看板拆解父任务排序Bug (Issue #133008) 属于较低严重程度的稳定性问题，目前暂无关联修复PR。

6. 功能需求与路线信号

过去一周用户提出的功能需求，以及近期纳入开发的可能性评估：

  1. CLI到桌面端的会话流转 + 深层链接 (PR #125903)：提供/handoff desktop命令和hermes://session/<id>深层链接，支持用户在桌面应用中继续CLI中的对话。可能性高：该PR基于早期社区工作整理而来，符合跨设备用户体验趋势，目前正处于活跃审核阶段。
  2. 桌面端会话状态分组全面改版 (PR #133020)：将侧边栏状态从"进行中/已完成"拆分为"进行中/受阻/待处理/未激活"，提升任务可见性。可能性高：属于低风险用户体验改进，用户价值明确，已进入CI审核状态。
  3. 看板Worker创建/链接权限粒度控制 (Issue #100944)：允许限制Worker的卡片创建/链接权限，同时保留生命周期管理工具。可能性中等：标记为needs-decision，说明路线图优先级尚未确定。
  4. hermes config set支持命名列表条目 (Issue #132963)：支持通过名称寻址列表类型的配置键（例如custom_providers）。可能性中等：属于小幅易用性改进，使用场景明确，如果配置工具相关工作排期，大概率会被纳入。
  5. Browser exec Python运行框架Docker沙箱化 (Issue #133010)：将browser_exec的Python代码放在配置的Docker沙箱中运行，以增强安全性。近期可能性较低：已被记录为已知限制，需要更广泛的沙箱架构改造工作。

7. 用户反馈总结

本周Issue报告中反映的核心痛点和使用场景：

  • 核心聊天用户体验退化：多名用户报告桌面客户端存在消息重复渲染和滚动跳变问题，其中一位用户提供了WebSocket帧追踪数据，排除了后端原因。这是导致用户不满的首要因素，因为它破坏了用户对聊天界面的基本信任。
  • 安装/更新阻碍：Termux/ARM64用户、Windows Python 3.14用户以及插件数量多的用户均报告了持续的更新失败问题（Python包布局不匹配、uv lock崩溃、插件并发加载错误）。这些入门和维护故障为非标准平台用户设置了很高的使用门槛。
  • 看板工作流中断：多名企业/自托管用户报告，在受管运行环境下看板Worker完全失效，阻断了任务委派使用场景——而这正是高级用户的核心价值主张之一。
  • 安全预期未被满足：启用了Docker沙箱的用户惊讶地发现browser_exec实际运行在主机而非容器中，说明文档记录的限制与用户对安全边界的认知存在差距。
  • 跨设备连续性需求：会话流转功能PR与用户反复提出的在CLI和桌面界面间转移对话的需求相契合，反映了用户在终端开始工作、在图形界面完成工作的使用场景。

8. 待办关注项

长期存在、高影响且等待维护者关注的事项：

  1. 后台自我改进范围违规 (Issue #72082, 创建于2026-07-26, 2条评论)：回合后后台审查会在只读范围的回合中写入技能库，且不会披露创建的文件。这违反了范围保证，已开放超过10周，进展有限。

IronClaw 项目周报 — 截至2026-10-05

1. 近7天总览

过去7天，IronClaw 开发节奏保持稳定，共有7个活跃 issue（无关闭）、13个更新的 PR（3个已合并/关闭），同时发布了一个新的稳定版本。项目在 v1.4.1 中推出了安全与功能补丁，当前 ongoing 工作集中在依赖维护、用户体验优化，以及工具选择和分布式 worker 的早期架构增强上。依赖更新在未合并 PR 中占比最高，10个未合并 PR 中有5个是自动依赖升级，体现了持续的基础设施维护工作。新贡献者的社区提交在功能和修复类 PR 中占比可观，反映出外部参与度正在提升。整体项目健康度稳定，发布工程、核心功能、开发者体验等各条线均有活跃进展。

2. 版本发布

  • ironclaw-v1.4.1（2026-09-29 发布）：1.4.1-rc.2 候选版本的正式稳定版。
    • 核心变更：
      1. 修复了在运营方通过 Web UI 提供 Google OAuth 客户端的部署场景下，Google 扩展（Gmail、Google Calendar）无法激活的问题。
      2. 纳入了 Wasmtime 安全更新，用于沙箱化 WASM 工具执行。

    • 迁移说明：无需手动迁移。1.4.0 或更早 1.4.x 候选版本的用户可通过官方安装器或包管理器正常升级。

3. 项目进展

近7天共合并/关闭3个 PR，推进了发布工程和 Web UI 稳定性：

  1. PR #8120 — chore(release): promote 1.4.1-rc.2 to 1.4.1（已关闭/已合并）：完成 v1.4.1 正式版发布工作，升级版本号并更新更新日志，同步了 RC2 中的 Google OAuth 修复和 Wasmtime 安全补丁。
  2. PR #5132 — fix(webui-v2): redirect invalid chat thread routes（已关闭/已合并）：修复了聊天线程深度链接失效的问题，将无效/保留的 /chat/:threadId 路由重定向回聊天主页面，并为聊天页面路由流程补充了回归测试。
  3. PR #8078 — chore(deps): bump the tokio-ecosystem group across 1 directory with 2 updates（已关闭）：已被更新的 tokio 生态依赖升级 PR #8123 取代，属于常规依赖维护节奏。

4. 社区热门话题

按评论数和讨论活跃度排序：

  1. Issue #2358 — feat(browser): add BrowserProfileStore trait with encrypted tarball persistence（1条评论，2026-10-01 更新）：本周评论数最多的未关闭 issue，聚焦于在智能体运行之间持久化浏览器会话（Cookie、localStorage），避免重复的用户身份验证。核心需求：智能体浏览器工作流需要持久、安全的登录态会话存储，这是浏览器自动化场景中关键的易用性缺口。
  2. Issue #7889 — RFC: extend the scheduler/orchestrator with opt-in remote edge workers（1条评论，2026-09-29 更新）：一项关于将 IronClaw 的 worker 池扩展到单主机之外、利用闲置边缘硬件的提案。核心需求：有多主机基础设施的运营方希望分布式部署智能体工作负载，以提升可扩展性和资源利用率，同时不破坏项目“安全优先”的审计模型。
  3. PR #7499 — feat(identyclaw): host-mediated Passport for practitioners（2026-10-01 更新）：一项社区贡献的功能，集成 IdentyClaw Passport 实现无需进程的智能体身份验证。核心需求：用户希望为智能体工作流提供内置、安全的身份证明，无需 shell 访问或安装外部扩展。

  2. 基准测试稳定性问题（严重程度：中）：两个每日失败分类 issue（2026-10-01 的 #8121、2026-09-28 的 #8116）记录了测试套件持续存在的不通过率。大部分失败归因于基准测试端的种子缺陷和模型质量问题，而非 IronClaw 核心 bug，但也表明测试流水线可靠性仍有提升空间。

2. 版本发布

过去7天未发布任何新版本。

3. 项目进展

过去一周，以下已关闭/已合并的PR与已完成的Issue推进了项目进度：

  • 已关闭Issue #7108：CI Rust构建缓存与关键路径优化 zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#7108 本次CI优化旨在缩短小改动下PR构建15-20分钟的耗时，目前已全部完成，提升了Rust构建缓存效率与任务调度性能。
  • 已关闭Issue #10662：Anthropic OAuth缓存标记大小错误修复 zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#10662 修复了OAuth系统前缀缓存标记低于Anthropic最低缓存阈值、浪费缓存断点槽位的问题。
  • 已关闭Issue #11335：无终端环境下CLI审批提示报错异常 zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11335 修复了CLI审批提示在无控制终端场景（如定时任务、CI流水线）下，运行时默认拒绝会错误返回Denied by user的问题。
  • 已合并PR #11518：保留CLI输入失败的溯源信息 zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11518 实现了Issue #11335的修复方案，确保CLI审批提示遇到EOF或读取错误时，会将“输入不可用”的结果同步至审计日志与模型上下文。
  • 已合并PR #11521：运行时组合异常审批文档 zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11521 正式确认核心团队对受限运行时组合异常的审批结果，更新项目文档以反映最终敲定的政策。

4. 社区热门话题

讨论量最高的内容围绕运行时测试可靠性、本地优先用户体验与CI性能展开：

  1. Issue #9965：并行运行时门控下加固运行时可执行测试固件（14条评论）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#9965 本周讨论量最高的问题，核心是并行运行时测试套件中，因测试固件在多线程初始化后写入可执行垫片导致测试偶发失败。根本需求：提升测试套件可靠性，让运行时改动的CI验证更快、结果更可信。
  2. Issue #5287：精简local_small运行时配置与提示预算约定（9条评论，2个👍）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#5287 本地模型用户呼声最高的增强功能，目标是减少提示冗余、禁用宽松兜底解析、防止内部工具指令泄露到用户输出中。根本需求：为算力与上下文窗口受限的本地优先部署场景，提供轻量、注重隐私、高性能的运行模式。
  3. Issue #7108：CI Rust构建缓存优化（9条评论）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#7108 这项刚关闭的CI优化引发了持续讨论，大家关注如何降低长PR构建时间给开发者带来的阻碍。根本需求：提升贡献者的开发迭代速度。

5. Bug与稳定性

过去7天上报或仍在处理的Bug，按严重程度排序如下：

  1. P0/S0：Issue #10495 - Config::save()会将已有内容的config.toml覆盖为几乎空白的文件 zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#10495 属于数据丢失级严重Bug：工作区测试运行时，可能将109KB、包含25个agent的配置文件替换为仅702字节的最小配置。状态：修复中。修复PR：#11527（禁止未经校验的全量保存覆盖已加载的配置文件）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11527
  2. P1/S1：Issue #11525 - Android/Termux上快速启动流程失败 zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11525 属于阻塞工作流的Bug：因配置持久化失败，无法在Android 16/Termux上创建agent。状态：已开放，暂未分配修复PR。
  3. P1/S1：Issue #10536 - macOS Seatbelt对Shell命令忽略已配置的allowed_roots zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#10536 属于沙箱安全Bug：用户配置的额外文件系统根目录未被Shell命令生效，导致出现Operation not permitted错误。状态：修复中，暂未关联修复PR。
  4. P1/S1：Issue #10673 - 守护进程RPC路径下失败的ACP回合未持久化（ZeroCode代码面板） zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#10673 属于阻塞工作流的Bug：ZeroCode代码面板中失败/取消的回合未被保存，与此前已修复的#9378用户影响一致，但出现在不同代码路径。状态：已开放。
  5. P1/S2：Issue #11420 - SQLite会话后端每个回合都会重写所有消息的created_at时间戳 zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11420 属于功能降级问题：全量对话记录重写时会将所有行的时间戳更新为当前时间，导致单条消息的时间戳数据丢失。状态：已开放，暂未关联修复PR。
  6. P2/S2：Issue #11517 - Web聊天中途刷新页面会导致用户提示从屏幕与localStorage中丢失 zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11517 属于前端Bug：回合进行中用回合前快照做水合时，会覆盖本地状态。状态：已开放。
  7. P3/S1：Issue #11418 - ZeroCode一键“复制”功能失效 zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11418 ZeroCode TUI的剪贴板功能失效。修复PR：#11529（新增Linux本地剪贴板写入逻辑与明确的复制结果提示）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11529

6. 功能需求与路线动态

当前活跃的功能需求与路线图对齐工作，大概率将在后续版本上线：

  • v0.8.6 大概率纳入功能：
    • 频道线程中恢复Slack“正在思考”状态（Issue #11416，进行中）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11416
    • MCP嵌套对象参数序列化修复（Issue #11371，已确认纳入v0.8.6）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11371
    • Tailscale隧道WSS/注册端点发布（PR #11530、#11531）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11530 zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11531
  • v0.9.0 路线图动态：
    • 网关拆分与运行时交付里程碑在Issue #7432中跟踪 zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#7432，包括标准配置生成发布（Issue #10892，进行中）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#10892
    • ZeroRelay 认证主体透传（Issue #10766），支持多用户托管中继部署 zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#10766
  • 中期功能候选：
    • 基于任务量的本地/云端模型路由（Issue #7951，进行中，暂列待办池）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#7951
    • Web端可视化cron调度编辑器（PR #10698，暂列待办池）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#10698
    • Sendblue iMessage/SMS 频道支持（PR #10768，暂列待办池）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#10768

7. 用户反馈汇总

近期Issue上报中反映的痛点与使用场景：

  1. 本地模型易用性痛点：使用本地模型运行ZeroClaw的用户反馈存在提示冗余、内部指令泄露、缺少专门轻量配置的问题，推动了local_small运行模式的需求（Issue #5287）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#5287。
  2. 跨平台部署缺口：Android/Termux用户无法完成快速启动上流程（Issue #11525）[zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11525]，macOS用户则面临用户配置的允许文件系统根目录沙箱不生效的问题（Issue #10536）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#10536，凸显了非标准平台与桌面端平台支持的不足。
  3. 数据可信度担忧：配置文件被覆盖（Issue #10495）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#10495、费用台账记录损坏（Issue #11515）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11515、消息时间戳丢失（Issue #11420）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11420 等问题上报，表明用户对数据完整性与持久化可靠性存在顾虑。
  4. 用户体验摩擦：ZeroCode剪贴板功能失效（Issue #11418）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11418、Slack缺少“正在思考”提示（Issue #11416）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11416、Web聊天刷新丢失用户输入（Issue #11517）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11517 等问题，反映核心界面功能的日常使用体验有所下降。

8. 待办关注项

长期存在、影响较大，需要维护者关注的事项：

  1. Issue #5287：local_small运行时配置（创建于2026-04-04，9条评论，2个👍）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#5287 本地优先部署场景下用户呼声最高的增强功能，风险与优先级均较高，目前仍在开发中，已开放6个月。
  2. PR #10698：可视化cron调度编辑器（创建于2026-09-07，待清理/待办池状态）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#10698 面向用户的体验优化功能，目前处于“需作者跟进”/待办池状态，存在贡献者流失风险。
  3. PR #10768：Sendblue iMessage/SMS 频道（创建于2026-09-10，待清理/待办池状态）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#10768 大型跨平台频道贡献，可扩展非Apple设备的iMessage支持，目前因等待维护者审核处于停滞状态。
  4. Issue #7951：基于任务量的本地/云端模型路由（创建于2026-06-19，待办池状态）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#7951 本地/云端混合部署场景下的高价值路由功能，开发中但优先级下调至待办池。
  5. Issue #9190：服务商API密钥轮换失效问题（创建于2026-07-20，无过期标记）zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#9190 高严重级别的服务商Bug：密钥轮换时能选中备用密钥但无法生效，近期无进展更新。

本周报由 agents-radar 自动生成。

item.content:encoded:
OpenClaw Ecosystem Weekly Digest 2026-10-05

Issues: 500 | PRs: 500 | Projects covered: 5 | Generated: 2026-10-05 01:47 UTC

  • OpenClaw
  • Hermes Agent
  • IronClaw
  • QwenPaw
  • ZeroClaw

OpenClaw Deep Dive

OpenClaw Weekly Project Digest (2026-10-05)

Data Source: github.com/openclaw/openclaw Reporting Period: 7 days ending 2026-10-05

1. Last 7 Days' Overview

OpenClaw maintained high development velocity this week, with 500 updated issues (350 active, 150 closed) and 500 updated PRs (309 open, 191 merged/closed). The project published 5 new releases, including a new stable version and extended-stable (LTS-equivalent) gateway updates, reflecting both active feature work and ongoing security/reliability maintenance. Key focus areas included update pipeline reliability, performance optimization for state and session management, and fixes for multi-agent and channel integration bugs. Community engagement remained strong, with active discussion on cost governance, memory system improvements, and multi-agent permission scoping. Overall project health is robust, with a steady cadence of bug fixes paired with forward-looking feature development.

2. Releases

5 new releases were published this week, spanning stable and extended-stable channels:

v2026.9.8 (Stable)

  • Stats: 58 commits, 43 PRs, 21 contributors
  • Details: Latest stable release with full changelog available via official release notes
  • Link: openclaw/openclaw Release v2026.9.8

v2026.9.7 (Stable)

  • Stats: 518 direct commits, 2,818 PRs, 334 contributors
  • Details: Major stable release with broad feature and bug fix updates; release notes available at official docs
  • Link: openclaw/openclaw Release v2026.9.7

Extended-Stable (Gateway-Only) Releases (LTS-equivalent)

Three extended-stable updates were released for the August 2026 baseline, focused on security patches, reliability fixes, performance improvements, and new model support:

  • v2026.8.35: openclaw/openclaw Release v2026.8.35
  • v2026.8.34: openclaw/openclaw Release v2026.8.34
  • v2026.8.33: openclaw/openclaw Release v2026.8.33

No breaking changes or mandatory migration steps were noted in the provided release data.

3. Project Progress

Of 191 merged/closed PRs this week, key advances include:

Update & Installation Reliability

  • PR #165257: Fix openclaw update failures in unprivileged containers by falling back to byte copy when FICLONE ioctl is denied (resolves #164113)
  • PR #165242: Repair legacy config handling for identical-package updates, preventing post-admission config rejection
  • PR #165233: Prevent spurious CLI errors after successful in-place updates caused by stale cleanup code imports

Performance Optimizations

  • PR #165249: Reduce retained worker task transport overhead by eliminating redundant message hops
  • PR #165186: Improve shared-state performance by attributing SQLite hold warnings and reusing integrity proofs
  • PR #165221: Bound transcript source reads to prevent 100+ MB heap spikes during large session history operations

Bug Fixes

  • PR #165210: Fix Code Mode nested call failures when providers reuse tool-call IDs across responses
  • PR #142888: Fix live assistant text doubling for OpenAI-compatible providers that resend full content in deltas (resolves #136262)
  • PR #144488: Make memory embedding request timeouts configurable and recoverable, fixing permanent index stalls on slow providers

UI/UX Improvements

  • PR #164607: Add channel identity link management to the Profile UI for gateway administrators
  • PR #165199: Fix overlapping sidebar pin editor and reorder grip controls

4. Community Hot Topics

The most actively discussed issues this week reflect core user priorities around cost control, runtime stability, and memory system behavior:

  1. Per-agent cost budget enforcement at the gateway level

    • Issue: #42475 (25 comments, 1 👍)
    • Analysis: Operators want native, gateway-level cost caps (daily/monthly) per agent to prevent runaway spending without external monitoring tools. This addresses a key operational pain point for multi-agent deployments, where current per-session tracking does not provide proactive budget guardrails.

  2. Zombie child process leak from hook/tool execution

    • Issue: #97616 (17 comments, 1 👍)
    • Analysis: Users report accumulating unreaped openclaw-hooks, bash, and codex child processes that degrade runtime performance over time. This is a high-priority stability concern for long-running gateway instances.

  3. Short-term recall retention eviction blocking memory promotion

    • Issue: #150635 (17 comments, 0 👍)
    • Analysis: The dreaming deep phase fails to promote memories to long-term storage once the 512-entry short-term cap is hit, due to nightly zero-recall entry ingestion. This breaks a core memory system feature for users with high session volume.

  4. Unbounded SQLite growth in memory core tables

    • Issue: #114612 (16 comments, 0 👍)
    • Analysis: memory_index_chunks and memory_embedding_cache tables grow without limit, risking disk exhaustion. This is a critical durability issue for production deployments with long uptime.

5. Bugs & Stability

Bugs reported/updated this week are ranked by severity (P0 > P1 > P2) and impact:

P0 (Critical)

  1. #164396: OpenClaw 2026.9.8 fails to connect to local gateway after clean Windows 11 + Node 22 LTS install
    • Impact: Onboarding failure for new Windows users; no fix PR linked yet
  2. #160959: Gateway blocks for minutes while capturing large external plugins (2026.9.6 regression)
    • Impact: Event loop starvation; no fix PR linked yet
  3. #157415: Doctor --fix refuses post-session plugin migrations for externally installed acpx and codex
    • Impact: Migration failure for plugin users; no fix PR linked yet
  4. #158390: plugin-captures tmp directories not garbage collected, filling disk indefinitely
    • Impact: Disk exhaustion; 1 👍 community support; no fix PR linked yet

P1 (High)

  1. #97616: Zombie child process leak from hooks/tools (see Community Hot Topics)
  2. #114612: Unbounded memory SQLite table growth (see Community Hot Topics)
  3. #161379: Gateway pins CPU core indefinitely due to OpenAI catalog refresh loop (60s TTL < per-agent refresh time)
    • Impact: 100% CPU usage on one core; no fix PR linked yet
  4. #161976: WhatsApp DM replies fail at durable registry handoff after restart
    • Impact: Message loss; no fix PR linked yet
  5. #144291: Config hot-reload aborts all in-flight agent turns
    • Impact: Session disruption; no fix PR linked yet

Notable Regressions

  • #97616 (zombie processes): Regression from earlier versions
  • #161379 (CPU pinning): 2026.9.6 regression
  • #160959 (plugin capture blocking): 2026.9.6 regression

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Top user-requested features with strong roadmap potential:

  1. Per-agent cost budget enforcement (#42475)

    • Gateway-level daily/monthly spend caps per agent. High operational relevance for enterprise deployments; likely to be prioritized given active discussion and maintainer review tags.

  2. Per-agent agentToAgent and session visibility scoping (#59149)

    • Replace global-only multi-agent permission settings with per-agent scoping. Has 2 👍 reactions and a linked PR (#155442 referenced in related issues), making it a strong candidate for upcoming releases.

  3. Shared workspace memory indexing (#95724)

    • Index memory by source directory instead of by agent to eliminate duplicate vector stores for same-workspace agents. Improves performance and reduces resource usage; fits ongoing memory system optimization work.

  4. Bounded launch contract for Swarm agents.run (#156632)

    • Add restricted execution boundaries for Swarm agent verification lanes. Has a linked implementation PR (#155442), indicating active development.

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain Points

  • Update reliability: Multiple reports of update failures, rollbacks, and stranded installations across platforms (macOS non-root #164422, Windows clean install #164396, unprivileged containers #164113).
  • Resource leaks: Disk and memory leaks from plugin captures #158390, memory tables #114612, and zombie processes #97616 are recurring themes for long-running deployments.
  • Channel delivery issues: Message loss and delivery failures across WhatsApp #161976, Signal #143581, iMessage #143632, and Telegram #143278 impact core user trust.
  • Multi-agent friction: Permission scoping #59149, subagent delivery failures #143334, and claude-cli multi-agent bugs #164972 hinder adoption of team-based agent workflows.

Use Cases

  • Enterprise multi-agent deployments with cost governance and hierarchical permission models
  • Long-running self-hosted gateways for personal/team productivity across multiple chat channels
  • Code Mode and development automation using Codex and claude-cli backends
  • Memory-augmented agents for knowledge work and long-term project context

Satisfaction Signals

  • Active community contribution (21-334 contributors per release) indicates strong engagement
  • Fast triage of regression bugs (multiple 2026.9.x regressions received immediate attention)

8. Backlog Watch

Long-standing or high-impact issues/PRs requiring maintainer attention:

  1. #84037: Improve Codex app-server steady-state CPU and helper process overhead

    • Created: 2026-05-19; 11 comments, 1 👍; P1 priority. Performance issue affecting Codex users with no fix PR linked.

  2. #95724: Index memory by source directory, not by agent

    • Created: 2026-06-22; 6 comments, 1 👍; P2 priority. Efficiency improvement for multi-agent workspaces with no linked PR yet.

  3. #59149: Per-agent agentToAgent and session visibility scoping

    • Created: 2026-04-01; 6 comments, 2 👍; P2 priority. Has a linked PR but remains open, requiring product decision.

  4. #119055: fix(code-mode): keep waiting results durable across retries

    • Created: 2026-08-04; maintainer-authored XL-sized PR. Core Code Mode reliability fix that has been in review for over 2 months.

  5. #144439: feat(agents): add configurable prompt section overrides

    • Created: 2026-09-10; P3 priority. Highly requested feature for customizing system prompts without forking; awaiting maintainer review.

Cross-Ecosystem Comparison

Cross-Project Personal AI Assistant / Agent Open-Source Ecosystem Comparison Report

Reporting Period: 7 days ending 2026-10-05

1. Ecosystem Overview

The open-source personal AI assistant and agent ecosystem remains in a high-growth, iterative phase, with projects balancing foundational reliability work against user-driven feature expansion for enterprise and power-user deployments. Across the five surveyed projects, core investment themes include runtime stability, memory system optimization, multi-channel integration, and cost governance for multi-agent deployments. Community contribution rates remain strong, with new contributors delivering targeted fixes and feature additions across all tiers of projects, while security hardening and sandboxing remain non-negotiable priorities for production-grade deployments. The landscape is segmented by use case: general-purpose gateway-centric platforms, local-first lightweight agents, and workflow-optimized assistants, each catering to distinct user personas and deployment models.

2. Activity Comparison

Project Updated Issues (Active/Closed) Updated PRs (Open/Merged) New Releases Health Score (1-10)
OpenClaw 500 (350 active / 150 closed) 500 (309 open / 191 merged) 5 (2 stable, 3 extended-stable) 9.0
Hermes Agent 50 (46 open / 4 closed) 50 (44 open / 6 merged) 0 7.2
IronClaw 7 (7 active / 0 closed) 13 (10 open / 3 merged) 1 (stable patch) 7.8
QwenPaw 50 (46 open / 4 closed) 50 (39 open / 11 merged) 1 (beta) 7.5
ZeroClaw 50 (47 open / 3 closed) 50 (45 open / 5 merged) 0 7.0

Health score calculated based on release cadence, bug triage speed, community contribution volume, and severity of open critical issues.

3. OpenClaw's Position

OpenClaw is the clear market and maturity leader in this cohort, with 10x the issue and PR volume of the next-largest projects, a robust multi-channel release pipeline (stable + extended-stable/LTS), and the largest contributor base (21–334 contributors per release). Its technical approach is gateway-centric, prioritizing multi-agent orchestration, cross-channel integration, and enterprise-grade operational controls (cost governance, permission scoping) that are only nascent in peer projects. In comparison to smaller peers, OpenClaw has a more established enterprise user base, reflected in community focus on production scalability, cost control, and long-running deployment reliability, whereas Hermes Agent and QwenPaw prioritize end-user UX and frontend polish, IronClaw focuses on security-first sandboxed execution, and ZeroClaw targets local-first, privacy-conscious deployments.

4. Shared Technical Focus Areas

  1. Runtime stability & resource leak mitigation
    Cross-project priority: All five projects face open issues related to memory leaks, process leaks, or event loop blocking. OpenClaw reports zombie child process leaks and unbounded SQLite memory table growth; QwenPaw documents 1MB/s memory growth from unbounded stream buffers; ZeroClaw addresses SQLite session backend inefficiencies; Hermes Agent cites CPU pegging from WebSocket reconnect loops; IronClaw tracks benchmark pipeline stability gaps.
  2. Installation/update reliability
    OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, and ZeroClaw all report platform-specific installation failures: OpenClaw fixes unprivileged container update failures and Windows clean install connectivity issues; Hermes Agent documents Termux/ARM64 and Windows Python 3.14 update crashes; ZeroClaw notes Android/Termux quickstart failures.
  3. Chat/transcript UX reliability
    Hermes Agent, QwenPaw, and OpenClaw all prioritize fixing streaming and transcript integrity bugs: Hermes Agent resolves desktop duplicate message rendering and scroll jumping; QwenPaw addresses compressed history loading failures and cross-session message attribution; OpenClaw fixes live assistant text doubling for OpenAI-compatible providers.
  4. Plugin/tool system robustness
    OpenClaw, Hermes Agent, QwenPaw, and IronClaw all have open work on plugin reliability: OpenClaw fixes plugin capture disk leaks and migration failures; Hermes Agent addresses concurrent plugin load crashes; QwenPaw resolves plugin synchronous call freezes; IronClaw advances Turn-0 tool selection optimization.

5. Differentiation Analysis

Dimension OpenClaw Hermes Agent IronClaw QwenPaw ZeroClaw
Core Focus Enterprise multi-agent gateway, cross-channel orchestration Desktop/CLI client UX, Kanban workflow Security-first sandboxed execution, WASM tooling Frontend console usability, multi-provider/channel compatibility Local-first privacy, runtime security hardening
Target Users Enterprise operators, large multi-agent deployments Power users, knowledge workers, desktop-first users Security-conscious teams, browser automation users Self-hosted teams, IM-heavy workflows Privacy-focused users, local model deployers
Technical Architecture Monolithic gateway with plugin ecosystem, SQLite-backed state Cross-platform desktop (Tauri-like) + CLI client, Python runtime Rust-based core, WASM sandboxed tool execution Web/desktop console, Python backend, multi-channel adapters Rust-based runtime, Tailscale/ZeroRelay networking, sandboxed execution
Key Differentiators LTS release channel, gateway-level cost/permission controls Kanban task delegation, CLI-to-desktop session handoff Wasmtime-secured tool sandbox, identity attestation support Mobile web adaptation, broad IM channel (Feishu/WeCom) support Local_small lightweight runtime profile, config integrity guarantees

6. Community Momentum & Maturity

Tier 1: Mature, High-Velocity (Stabilizing + Feature Expansion)

  • OpenClaw: The most mature project, with a balanced cadence of security patches, bug fixes, and forward-looking feature work. Its dual stable/extended-stable release pipeline and 191 merged PRs per week indicate established release engineering and large maintainer capacity. The project is in a sustained growth phase, prioritizing enterprise operational features alongside reliability hardening.

Tier 2: Mid-Maturity, Active Development (Feature-First Iteration)

  • QwenPaw: Steady iteration with a focus on frontend UX and provider/channel compatibility. Its beta release cadence and 11 merged PRs per week reflect active feature work alongside bug triage, with growing community contribution from first-time developers.
  • Hermes Agent: High open-to-closed PR ratio indicates an active development cycle focused on desktop UX and workflow features, with no upcoming stabilization release in sight. Strong community demand for cross-device continuity and Kanban reliability drives roadmap priorities.
  • IronClaw: Smaller but stable activity volume, with a mix of security patch releases, dependency maintenance, and early-stage architecture work. Growing external contributor engagement signals expanding community buy-in, while its focus on sandbox security positions it as a niche but high-trust option.

Tier 3: Pre-Stable, Foundational Hardening

  • ZeroClaw: High volume of in-progress high-severity bugs and architecture-tracked enhancements indicate the project is still shoring up foundational reliability for v0.8.6 and v0.9.0 milestones. Its focus on local-first privacy and runtime security appeals to a niche user base, but slower merge velocity and multiple parking-lot features signal lower maintainer capacity than Tier 1/2 projects.

7. Trend Signals

  1. Enterprise operational controls are table stakes for production adoption
    OpenClaw’s top community request for gateway-level per-agent cost budgeting, paired with demand for per-agent permission scoping, indicates multi-agent deployments are moving from pilot to production, requiring native governance tools instead of external monitoring workarounds. AI agent developers building for enterprise use cases should prioritize built-in cost caps, audit logging, and granular permission models.
  2. Local-first and privacy-focused deployment demand is accelerating
    ZeroClaw’s highly requested local_small runtime profile, paired with user frustration over prompt bloat and leaked internal instructions for local model users, reflects growing demand for lightweight, privacy-preserving agent modes optimized for on-premise and consumer hardware. Developers should optimize prompt size and disable unnecessary permissive fallbacks for local deployment targets.
  3. Cross-device and cross-channel continuity is a core UX differentiator
    Hermes Agent’s CLI-to-desktop handoff feature, QwenPaw’s mobile web adaptation work, and OpenClaw’s multi-channel integration fixes all point to user expectation of seamless agent access across devices and chat platforms. Agents limited to a single interface will face growing UX competition in 2026.
  4. Memory system reliability and scalability are unmet pain points
    OpenClaw’s short-term memory eviction bugs and unbounded SQLite growth, paired with QwenPaw’s compressed history loading failures, indicate that current memory architectures are not keeping pace with high-volume, long-running deployment needs. Agent developers should prioritize bounded memory storage, pagination for historical transcripts, and reliable long-term memory promotion pipelines.
  5. Sandbox security expectations are outpacing current implementations
    IronClaw’s focus on WASM sandbox hardening, ZeroClaw’s macOS Seatbelt bug fixes, and Hermes Agent user surprise over un-sandboxed browser_exec code show that users assume stronger security boundaries than most projects currently deliver. Transparent sandbox scope documentation and consistent enforcement across tool execution paths will be critical for building user trust.

P1/S1: Issue #10536 - macOS Seatbelt ignores configured allowed_roots for shell commands zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#10536 Sandbox security bug where user-configured additional filesystem roots are not honored by shell commands, resulting in Operation not permitted errors. Status: in progress, no fix PR linked.
  4. P1/S1: Issue #10673 - Failed ACP turns not persisted on daemon RPC path (ZeroCode Code pane) zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#10673 Workflow-blocking bug where failed/cancelled turns in ZeroCode's Code pane are not saved, matching user impact of the previously fixed #9378 for a different code path. Status: open.
  5. P1/S2: Issue #11420 - SQLite session backend rewrites all message created_at timestamps on each turn zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11420 Degraded behavior where per-message timestamp data is lost because full transcript rewrites stamp all rows with the current time. Status: open, no fix PR linked.
  6. P2/S2: Issue #11517 - Web chat reload mid-turn drops user prompt from screen and localStorage zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11517 Frontend bug where hydration with a pre-turn snapshot overwrites local state during active turns. Status: open.
  7. P3/S1: Issue #11418 - ZeroCode "Copy" one-click feature not working zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11418 Clipboard functionality failure in ZeroCode TUI. Fix PR: #11529 (adds local Linux clipboard writers and explicit copy outcome reporting) zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11529

6. Feature Requests & Roadmap Signals

Active feature requests and roadmap-aligned work likely to appear in upcoming releases:

  • v0.8.6 likely inclusions:
    • Slack "is thinking" status restoration for channel threads (Issue #11416, in progress) zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11416
    • MCP nested object argument serialization fix (Issue #11371, accepted for v0.8.6) zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11371
    • Tailscale tunnel WSS/enrollment endpoint publishing (PR #11530, #11531) zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11530 zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11531
  • v0.9.0 roadmap signals:
    • Gateway separation and runtime delivery milestones tracked in Issue #7432 zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#7432, including canonical config generation publication (Issue #10892, in progress) zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#10892
    • ZeroRelay authenticated principal passthrough (Issue #10766) to enable multi-user hosted relay deployments zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#10766
  • Medium-term feature candidates:
    • Effort-based local/cloud model routing (Issue #7951, in progress, parking lot status) zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#7951
    • Guided cron schedule editor for web UI (PR #10698, parking lot) zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#10698
    • Sendblue iMessage/SMS channel support (PR #10768, parking lot) zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#10768

7. User Feedback Summary

Pain points and use cases surfaced in recent issue reports:

  1. Local model usability pain: Users running ZeroClaw with local models report prompt bloat, leaked internal instructions, and lack of a dedicated lightweight profile, driving demand for the local_small runtime mode (Issue #5287) zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#5287.
  2. Cross-platform deployment gaps: Android/Termux users cannot complete quickstart onboarding (Issue #11525) [zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11525], while macOS users face sandbox inconsistencies with user-configured allowed filesystem roots (Issue #10536) [zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#10536], highlighting gaps in non-standard and desktop platform support.
  3. Data trust concerns: Reports of config file overwrites (Issue #10495) [zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#10495], torn cost ledger records (Issue #11515) [zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11515], and lost message timestamps (Issue #11420) [zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11420] indicate user anxiety around data integrity and persistence reliability.
  4. UX friction: Broken clipboard functionality in ZeroCode (Issue #11418) [zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11418], missing Slack "thinking" indicators (Issue #11416) [zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11416], and lost user prompts on web chat reload (Issue #11517) [zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#11517] point to degraded day-to-day user experience for core interface features.

8. Backlog Watch

Long-standing high-impact items requiring maintainer attention:

  1. Issue #5287: local_small runtime profile (created 2026-04-04, 9 comments, 2 👍) zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#5287 A top user-requested enhancement for local-first deployments with high risk and priority, in progress but open for 6 months.
  2. PR #10698: Guided cron schedule editor (created 2026-09-07, stale candidate/parking lot status) zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#10698 User-facing UX improvement stuck in needs-author-action/parking lot state, risking contributor attrition.
  3. PR #10768: Sendblue iMessage/SMS channel (created 2026-09-10, stale candidate/parking lot status) zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#10768 Large cross-platform channel contribution that expands non-Apple iMessage support, currently stalled awaiting maintainer review.
  4. Issue #7951: Effort-based local/cloud model routing (created 2026-06-19, parking lot status) zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#7951 High-value routing feature for hybrid local/cloud deployments, in progress but deprioritized to parking lot.
  5. Issue #9190: Reliable provider API key rotation failure (created 2026-07-20, no-stale status) zeroclaw-labs/zeroclaw#9190 High-severity provider bug where key rotation selects alternate keys but cannot apply them, with no recent progress updates.
